title: 24.2 A 14b 1GS/s Single-Channel Pipelined ADC with A Parallel-Operation SAR Sub-Quantizer and A Dynamic-Deadzone Ring Amplifier
problem: Pipelined ADCs with ≥1GS/s speed and ≥14b resolution suffer from high power consumption due to multi-stage residue amplifiers and flash quantizers; using a single-channel SAR sub-quantizer reduces overhead but creates timing pressure that forces high-power amplifiers, or conversely, accepting reduced input swing.
motivation: High-resolution high-speed ADCs are essential for wireless communications and instrumentation; reducing power per conversion step while maintaining SNDR directly improves system-on-chip power efficiency.
method: This 14-bit, 1-gigahertz analog-to-digital converter runs amplification and quantization (precision measurement) in parallel within a pipeline. While one stage performs successive approximation—testing increasingly accurate guesses to convert an analog signal to a digital value—the residual amplifier for the next stage simultaneously amplifies the prior measurement's error. This parallelization eliminates the timing pressure that normally forces amplifiers to be fast and power-hungry. The amplifier uses a ring topology with dynamic-deadzone biasing (self-adjusting circuitry for temperature and voltage variations), avoiding manual per-chip tuning.
key_novelty: Overlapping successive-approximation conversion (testing increasingly precise guesses) with residual amplification to eliminate timing constraints, enabling lower-power amplifier design without sacrificing signal quality or input range.
contributions: Parallel-operation SAR scheme that overlaps conversion and amplification, reducing stage count and power
Dynamic-deadzone ring amplifier with improved linearity and PVT-robustness compared to conventional ring amplifiers
Single-channel design achieving 68.2 dB SNDR at Nyquist with 15.3 mW power consumption
Schreier FoM of 173.3 dB demonstrating power-efficient high-resolution architecture
baselines: conventional pipelined ADC with flash quantizers
limitations: Area breakdown and relative comparison of ring-amplifier power contribution not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Power-efficient 14b 1GS/s pipelined ADC using parallel SAR sub-conversion and dynamic ring amplifier
